summary: The appeals concerned the legality and effect of delay in executing the death sentence awarded to convicts in a rarest of the rare case involving rape and murder. The convicts were sentenced to death by the Sessions Court in 2012, confirmed by the Bombay High Court in 2012 and upheld by the Supreme Court in 2015. Subsequent delays occurred in processing mercy petitions before the Governor and President, with procedural lapses in document submission and communication. The convicts filed mercy petitions, both were rejected, but significant time lapsed due to administrative delays. The state sought execution of the sentence, while the convicts argued that prolonged delay warranted commutation. The Court examined whether inordinate delay in execution, attributable to the state, violates Article 21 and considered precedent on death row phenomenon. The Court emphasized that while delay alone does not mandate commutation, if it results from state inaction or misconduct and causes mental agony, it may warrant relief.
legal_provisions_cited: Art. 21 of the Constitution of India
Landmark case: Shatrughan Chauhan v. Union of India (2014)
final_judgment: The appeal was disposed of with directions to the authorities to ensure no further delay in execution, while affirming that the delay in this case, though substantial, did not warrant commutation of the death sentence given the gravity of the offence and absence of intentional delay by the state to prejudice the convicts.
